method: Luminance-conditioned chroma quantile transfer applied after frozen JPEG generation. Predict the color distribution of shadows, midtones and highlights without spatial shifts, VAE latents, local-mean grid adjustment or a new object decoder.
training: Use the 512 existing unrelated personal calibration categories, ten photos and four EEG trials per photo. No session-matched panel category belongs to these 512. For each cropped RGB photo measure the 15th, 50th and 85th percentiles of B-minus-Y and R-minus-Y in each of four within-photo luminance-rank quarters at 64x64 (BT.601 Y). Empty quarters use the whole photograph. Regress 24 within-object-centered coordinates from standardized 1003-dimensional posterior EEG, ridge 0.3 times the number of fitting rows. Estimate a single shrinkage in [0,1] from true versus predicted within-object deviations on the previously registered 416/96 generic split. Refit ridge on all 512. No target panels select any setting.
conditions: On each registered fold use the same previously generated own-EEG JPEG as the source for every arm. Keep its frozen word, crop, edges and query row. The palette prior averages the 24 measurements from that predicted object's eight allowed support photos. Subtract those eight EEG predictions' mean from the query prediction. For the cohort take the arithmetic mean of the three separately learned, shrinkage-scaled deviations on the same eight supports. Wrong reassigns the residual using the native frozen donor with the same predicted word and fold.
transform: For each luminance quarter independently, linearly interpolate the difference between target and source chroma quantiles, sorting target quantiles to enforce monotonicity. Average tied source knots. Keep the outermost difference constant beyond the 15th/85th percentile. Interpolate the four curves over per-pixel luminance rank; apply half their displacement, clipping each displacement before halving to 0.12. Preserve BT.601 luminance by corresponding green compensation and reduce any out-of-gamut displacement uniformly to the nearest valid RGB. Save neutral re-encode, support prior, own and wrong with identical quality-95 4:4:4 JPEG settings. Original source remains identifiable by SHA.
test: Both already-studied session-matched panels (stress12 and new_three4), fixed sub-04 and the three-person twelve-presentation acquisition. This is a post-hoc method evaluation on these panels. Inference uses only fold-permitted support colors and EEG; original query images are separated by stage and used only to score the completed JPEGs. All rows, including incorrect words, are included.
primary: Mean 32x32 position-matched Euclidean distance in perceptual OKLab a,b (multiply by 100). Lower is better. Compare reopened own JPEG against neutral, support prior and same-word wrong EEG. Also report RGB RMSE and spatial BT.601 luminance correlation, with strict wrong-EEG subset requiring distinct donor, same true object, word and fold. Per-panel paired 95% intervals resample the 12 complete objects 10000 times, seed 260541. Two readouts measured on common photos are reported separately and never treated as independent subjects.
secondary: Independent frozen DINOv2-S/14 same-object ten-photo identification for the four actual JPEG arms, using the legacy panel centering. A change in color agreement alone does not establish a gain in object recognition or identity.
decision: No method promotion unless own beats neutral and support prior on primary color error in both panels for the single-person task with 95% confidence bounds excluding zero and correct-source residual beats the valid same-object donor control in both. Leave an unsuccessful result as a color diagnostic.
